chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, the brother of Hisham, from Amr ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah, in every night of the month of Ramadan, are those freed from the Fire, except for one who breaks his fast with an intoxicant, or one who is malicious/ill-tempered, and the owner of the two fingers (chess). I asked: And what is the owner of the two fingers? He said: Chess.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الشَّاهَیْنِ: Owner of the two fingers (a reference to chess)

ai.seo_question: Who is excluded from the nightly freeing from Hell during Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition to highlight the daily spiritual liberation granted by Allah during Ramadan, emphasizing that this mercy is contingent upon specific behavioral exclusions. The unique mention of chess ('owner of the two fingers') reflects the classical scholarly view on games of chance and distraction as impediments to spiritual presence, while the 'malicious disposition' underscores the importance of inner character alongside ritual observance.
